preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 500 for line in stdin.splitlines()[:2]) and all(0 <= int(h) <= 999 for line in stdin.splitlines()[2:] for h in line.split())
preconditions.description: The first two lines of stdin contain integers x and y (1 ≤ x, y ≤ 500), followed by y lines of x integers each (0 ≤ h_ij ≤ 999) representing the garden's height profile.
The number of lines in stdin is exactly 2 (for x and y) plus y (for the height grid).

postconditions.expression: stdout.isdigit() and (int(stdout) == sum(1 for i in range(y) for j in range(x) if is_local_minimum(i, j)))
postconditions.description: stdout is a non-negative integer equal to the count of cells (i, j) where water can pool, i.e., cells that are local minima in their 4-neighborhood (no adjacent cell has strictly lower height).

invariants.description: x and y are the dimensions of the grid, derived from the first two lines of stdin.

invariants.expression: grid := [[int(h) for h in line.split()] for line in stdin.splitlines()[2:]]
invariants.description: grid is a 2D list of integers representing the height profile, where grid[i][j] is the height of cell (i, j).

invariants.expression: is_local_minimum := lambda i, j: all(grid[i][j] <= grid[ni][nj] for ni, nj in [(i-1,j), (i+1,j), (i,j-1), (i,j+1)] if 0 <= ni < y and 0 <= nj < x)
invariants.description: A cell (i, j) is a local minimum if its height is less than or equal to all its 4-adjacent neighbors (within grid bounds).
